Hi Samir —

Thanks for the quick response. Answers inline below, and I've attached the subprocessor CSV + SOC 2 report stub for your review.

---
Q: PHI & GDPR
A: Per your note, PHI is not in scope on day 1. If you later plan to send PHI, Redwood supports BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we evaluate on a case-by-case basis and often recommend Private deployment or a contract-level BAA. We can have legal follow up with your counsel; I've looped Rishi to coordinate.

Q: SOC 2
A: Attached: "SOC2_Report_2026-12.pdf" (redacted executive summary). If you need the full report, we can provide a secure view link under NDA/LOA.

Q: Cloud providers & regions
A: Primary hosting for Redwood Hosted API is AWS (us-west-2 & us-east-1) with optional GCP for dedicated/private deployments. We replicate only as configured per customer routing policy — for Acme we can restrict to US regions only.

Q: Subprocessors & access to plaintext
A: Attached CSV: "redwood_subprocessors_v2.csv". Key entries called out below:
- AWS (Amazon Web Services) — core compute & storage — may handle encrypted and transient plaintext in-memory during inference; access limited to infra admin roles; logs are accessible to support under controlled process.
- Datadog — monitoring/metrics only (no plaintext customer content).
- Sentry — error monitoring (sanitized stack traces; no customer payload stored by default).
- Segment (analytics) — opt-in for usage analytics; only metadata, not customer payload unless explicitly enabled.

We can flag any of those for you if Acme wants to disallow specific providers. For logging: by default we keep short-lived traces for debugging (redacted where possible); retention can be configured and we support strict no-logging policies on Dedicated/Private deployments.
